Lots of reductionist reactions to this. 

Lots of people here acting like parties or first past the post are the problems and just getting rid of either of them be a panacea.

I'm not necessarily against those but I want people to recognize that parties and first past the post didn't get added recently.

During the first part of this gif we had both of those and we had plenty of bipartisanship.

We have to ask ourselves what changed.

Why are we more divided and more tribal than we were 50 years ago?

I don't have the answer, but just know that if it was easy to fix it probably already would have. This is a hard problem that probably can't be fixed by one person.

It requires coordination and it requires we actually understand the problem.

I'll put my hot takes down here. Wanted to keep the top level comment strong by avoiding speculation I don't have evidence for. 

I see getting rid of FPTP as a way to increase representation by giving us more alternatives when voting but it doesn't seem evident to me that it would solve the problem. Not that I think it would be a bad thing but Reddit sees it as more of a silver bullet than it would be.

We are much more tribal than we used to be and I agree that it's probably in part due to the media.

There was a shift in how the parties operated in the 70s. I think the Wikipedia article on polarization talks about it. It's a pretty good intro but of course doesn't put forth many solutions

His argument isn't invalidated because he used the word toxic masculinity.

1) All terminology is made up at one point
2) [Toxic Masculinity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toxic_masculinity) is an accepted term that is researched in psychology.

From wikipedia
>[Toxic Masculinity] refer[s] to certain norms of masculine behavior in North America and Europe that are associated with harm to society and to men themselves.

Even if you don't like the term, what is being described isn't inconceivable and we should be able to discuss it. It sounds like what you're doing here is constructing a bunch of straw men.

Instead, try to create the strongest version of *their* argument, something so good that they wish they had come up with it, and then show why their position doesn't hold water.

I appreciate the amount of maturity you're showing with your response. Online forums can often be very toxic. Personally I have no horse in the race one way or the other. I don't have time to read the discussion up to this point (as I'm in the middle of moving!) and just wanted to take a small amount of time to try to help improve the discourse.

I think Reddit is at its best when people are thoughtful and making strong arguments, so I just wanted to try to help where I can.



Side note: I see what you mean about the usage of terms. People often use certain language to signal to their own camp "I'm one of you guys".
 
Someone unironically using the term toxic masculinity is definitely telling you something about that person.

But, in my opinion, this information should only be used to tell you how to best try to persuade that person. If it tells you something about their assumptions, and those assumptions are wrong and invalidate their argument, try to take it in that direction.

I wish you the best and hope you have a good day.
